* Challenges:
  + Selectivity needs to be scale invariant
  + Need to avoid circularity in the definition of cell populations
  + Need a sufficiently flexible model to consider many possible ligand designs
  + Need to account for differences in sample sizes across cell types
  + Need Invariance with respect to cell sampling
  + Need scalability into multiple dimensions
* Distribution shape metrics are effective for screening low dimensional targets (strong correlation with EMD, binding model) but are not applicable to target pairs/triads (@suppfig-distribution-features)
* EMD and KL are scale invariant (@fig-scale-invariance), but are highly dependent on the relative size of target and off-target populations (@fig-targ-prop-kldiv and @fig-targ-prop-emd) and cell sample size (@fig-bootstrap-kldiv and @fig-bootstrap-emd).
* Binding model is more consistent across cell subsamples (@fig-bootstrap-selec), more flexible (@fig-figure-1), and is invariant with respect to relative size of target and off-target populations (@fig-targ-prop-selec), but is not scale invariant (in >1D) (@suppfig-2d-scale-invariance).
* Binding model selectivity is not perfectly correlated with W or KL (@fig-scan-comp).
  + KL outliers are driven by singular outliers in target receptor expression
  + EMD outlier pairs capture simple single-receptor differences
  + Binding model outliers are infrequent and don’t obscure top hits
* Binding model predictions align with validated multi-specific targeting schemes?
* Binding model is more robust in terms of the challenges of the problem, is more robust in terms of outliers, and holds more biological relevance/interpretability
